# anyscale_scheduler_config (Resource)

Manages the [Anyscale Scheduler](https://docs.anyscale.com/scheduler) configuration for your organization: the resource flavors, resource queues, scheduling rules, and recycle policy that govern how workloads are admitted and where they run.

~> **Beta.** The Anyscale Scheduler is a beta product and its configuration fields may change. Applying a scheduler config changes how *every* workload in the organization is admitted - a scheduling rule that matches no queue, or a `nominal_quota` of `0`, can prevent workloads from starting. Review [the product documentation](https://docs.anyscale.com/scheduler) before your first apply.

~> **Singleton, authoritative-write.** An organization has at most one active scheduler config, and this resource owns the whole document - there is no per-cloud variant and no user-chosen key. Two Terraform configurations that both declare `anyscale_scheduler_config` for the same organization will silently fight, each apply reverting the other. Declare it in exactly one place. Changes made outside Terraform (CLI or console) appear as drift and are reverted by the next apply.

~> **`terraform destroy` does not clear the configuration.** The Anyscale API has no delete operation for scheduler configs, so destroying this resource removes it from Terraform state while the organization's config stays active. See the warning emitted at destroy time.

Requires the Anyscale Scheduler to be enabled for your organization. If it is not, the provider reports that explicitly rather than surfacing a bare permission error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The Anyscale Scheduler configuration is a single document per organization.
# Declare it in exactly one Terraform configuration: this resource owns the
# whole document, so a second configuration managing it would revert the first.

resource "anyscale_scheduler_config" "this" {
  # Named hardware profiles that queues allocate quota against.
  resource_flavors = [
    {
      name = "cpu-standard"
      selector = [
        {
          key      = "node.kubernetes.io/instance-type"
          operator = "in"
          values   = ["m5.4xlarge", "m5.8xlarge"]
        },
      ]
    },
    {
      name = "gpu-a10"
      selector = [
        {
          key      = "accelerator"
          operator = "in"
          values   = ["A10G"]
        },
      ]
    },
  ]

  # Queues that workloads are admitted into. Both queues share a cohort, so
  # unused quota in one is available to the other.
  resource_queues = [
    {
      name        = "batch"
      cohort_name = "shared"

      preemption = {
        within_resource_queue = "lower_priority"
        reclaim_within_cohort = "any"
        borrow_within_cohort  = "lower_priority"
      }

      resource_groups = [
        {
          covered_resources = ["cpu", "memory_gb"]
          flavors = [
            {
              name = "cpu-standard"
              resources = [
                { name = "cpu", nominal_quota = 256 },
                { name = "memory_gb", nominal_quota = 1024 },
              ]
            },
          ]
        },
        {
          covered_resources = ["gpu"]
          flavors = [
            {
              name = "gpu-a10"
              # Omitting nominal_quota means unlimited. An explicit 0 would
              # block GPUs for this queue entirely - the two are not the same.
              resources = [
                { name = "gpu", borrowing_limit = 8 },
              ]
            },
          ]
        },
      ]
    },
    {
      name        = "interactive"
      cohort_name = "shared"

      resource_groups = [
        {
          covered_resources = ["cpu", "memory_gb"]
          flavors = [
            {
              name = "cpu-standard"
              resources = [
                { name = "cpu", nominal_quota = 64, lending_limit = 32 },
                { name = "memory_gb", nominal_quota = 256 },
              ]
            },
          ]
        },
      ]
    },
  ]

  # Rules are evaluated top to bottom and the first match wins. Once any rule
  # exists, a workload matching none of them is rejected, so the last rule here
  # is a deliberate catch-all.
  scheduling_rules = [
    {
      selector = [
        {
          key      = "workload-type"
          operator = "in"
          values   = ["notebook", "workspace"]
        },
      ]
      resource_queue = "interactive"

      priority_policy = {
        default      = 100
        min          = 50
        max          = 200
        on_violation = "reject"
      }
    },
    {
      resource_queue = "batch"
    },
  ]

  recycle_policy = {
    rotation_interval = "24h"
    max_idle_duration = "10m"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `recycle_policy` (Attributes) When the scheduler retires and replaces the machines it manages. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--recycle_policy))
- `resource_flavors` (Attributes List) Named hardware profiles that queues allocate quota against. Order is significant: when a workload can run on more than one flavor, flavors are tried in the order written here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource_flavors))
- `resource_queues` (Attributes List) Queues that workloads are admitted into, each carrying its own quota and preemption policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource_queues))
- `scheduling_rules` (Attributes List) Rules mapping workloads to queues. **First match wins, top to bottom**, so order is significant. Once any rule exists, a workload matching no rule is rejected rather than run unscheduled - keep a catch-all rule last unless that is what you intend. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scheduling_rules))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When this config version was applied, RFC 3339.
- `creator_id` (String) ID of the user that applied this config version. May be `null` for versions applied by an automated process that the API does not attribute to a user.
- `version` (Number) Version number of the scheduler config this state represents. Config documents are immutable and monotonically versioned: every apply mints a new version rather than editing the previous one.

<a id="nestedatt--recycle_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `recycle_policy`

Optional:

- `max_idle_duration` (String) How long a machine may sit idle before being reclaimed, as a duration string (for example `10m`).
- `max_workloads` (Number) How many workloads a machine may run before being rotated out.
- `rotation_interval` (String) How long a machine may serve before being rotated out, as a duration string (for example `24h`).


<a id="nestedatt--resource_flavors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_flavors`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the flavor, referenced by `resource_queues[].resource_groups[].flavors[].name`.

Optional:

- `advanced_instance_config` (String) Cloud-provider-specific instance configuration applied to machines in this flavor, as a JSON string. Use `jsonencode()` for HCL objects. This can't be a native/dynamic value: it lives inside a list, and Terraform doesn't support a dynamic type nested inside a list - the same constraint that shapes `advanced_instance_config` on `anyscale_compute_config`. Compared semantically rather than by text, so key order and whitespace never produce a diff - `{"a":1,"b":2}` and `{ "b":2, "a":1 }` are the same value. Numbers are compared as written, so `1` and `1.0` are *not* the same value; `jsonencode()` avoids the question entirely.
- `selector` (Attributes List) Node label expressions selecting the machines this flavor covers. All expressions must match (AND). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource_flavors--selector))

<a id="nestedatt--resource_flavors--selector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_flavors.selector`

Required:

- `key` (String) Label key to match on the node.
- `operator` (String) How `key` is compared: `in` and `not_in` test membership in `values`; `exists` and `does_not_exist` test only for the key's presence and take no `values`.

Optional:

- `values` (List of String) Values compared against `key`. Required for `in` and `not_in`; must be omitted for `exists` and `does_not_exist`.



<a id="nestedatt--resource_queues"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_queues`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the queue, referenced by `scheduling_rules[].resource_queue`.

Optional:

- `cohort_name` (String) Cohort this queue belongs to. Queues in the same cohort can lend and borrow unused quota from one another; a queue with no cohort never shares quota.
- `preemption` (Attributes) When workloads in this queue may be preempted to make room for others. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource_queues--preemption))
- `resource_groups` (Attributes List) Quota for this queue, grouped by the resource types each group governs. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource_queues--resource_groups))

<a id="nestedatt--resource_queues--preemption"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_queues.preemption`

Optional:

- `borrow_within_cohort` (String) Whether this queue may preempt workloads in other queues of its cohort in order to borrow quota beyond its own: `never` or `lower_priority`.
- `reclaim_within_cohort` (String) Whether this queue may preempt workloads in other queues of its cohort to reclaim quota it lent out: `never`, `lower_priority`, or `any`.
- `within_resource_queue` (String) Whether a workload in this queue may preempt another workload in the same queue: `never` or `lower_priority`.


<a id="nestedatt--resource_queues--resource_groups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_queues.resource_groups`

Required:

- `covered_resources` (List of String) Resource types this group governs, lowercase (`cpu`, `gpu`, `memory_gb`, `tpu` at the time of writing; accelerator names are added over time, so this list is not fixed here). An unsupported value is reported at plan time by the Anyscale API, which returns the authoritative list.
- `flavors` (Attributes List) Per-flavor quota within this group. Order is significant - flavors are tried in the order written. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource_queues--resource_groups--flavors))

<a id="nestedatt--resource_queues--resource_groups--flavors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_queues.resource_groups.flavors`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of a flavor declared in `resource_flavors`.

Optional:

- `resources` (Attributes List) Quota for each covered resource type on this flavor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource_queues--resource_groups--flavors--resources))

<a id="nestedatt--resource_queues--resource_groups--flavors--resources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_queues.resource_groups.flavors.resources`

Required:

- `name` (String) Resource type this quota applies to. Must be one of the enclosing group's `covered_resources`.

Optional:

- `borrowing_limit` (Number) Most this queue may borrow from its cohort beyond `nominal_quota`. Omit for no limit; `0` borrows nothing.
- `lending_limit` (Number) Most of `nominal_quota` this queue will lend to other queues in its cohort. Omit for no limit; `0` lends nothing.
- `nominal_quota` (Number) Quota guaranteed to this queue for this resource. Omit for unlimited. **`0` is not the same as omitting it**: an explicit `0` blocks this resource entirely for this queue.





<a id="nestedatt--scheduling_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scheduling_rules`

Required:

- `resource_queue` (String) Name of the queue matching workloads are admitted into. Must name a queue declared in `resource_queues`.

Optional:

- `priority_policy` (Attributes) Priority bounds applied to workloads matched by this rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scheduling_rules--priority_policy))
- `selector` (Attributes List) Workload label expressions this rule matches on. All expressions must match (AND). Omit for a catch-all rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scheduling_rules--selector))

<a id="nestedatt--scheduling_rules--priority_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scheduling_rules.priority_policy`

Optional:

- `default` (Number) Priority assigned to a matching workload that requests none.
- `max` (Number) Highest priority a matching workload may request.
- `min` (Number) Lowest priority a matching workload may request.
- `on_violation` (String) What to do with a workload requesting a priority outside `min`/`max`: `reject` it, or `force_update` its priority to the nearest bound.


<a id="nestedatt--scheduling_rules--selector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scheduling_rules.selector`

Required:

- `key` (String) Label key to match on the workload.
- `operator` (String) How `key` is compared: `in` and `not_in` test membership in `values`; `exists` and `does_not_exist` test only for the key's presence and take no `values`.

Optional:

- `values` (List of String) Values compared against `key`. Required for `in` and `not_in`; must be omitted for `exists` and `does_not_exist`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The scheduler config is a singleton per organization, so it is imported by
# organization ID. The ID must match the organization the provider's token
# authenticates to - the anyscale_organization data source reports it.
terraform import anyscale_scheduler_config.this org_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
```
